description: A global flash drought inventory based on soil moisture volatility is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Mahmoud Osman et al. Flash droughts, characterized by rapid onset and development, present significant challenges to agriculture and climate mitigation strategies. Operational drought monitoring systems, based on precipitation, soil moisture deficits, or temperature anomalies, often fail to detect these events in time. Identification and monitoring indices need to account for the rapid onset of flash droughts. Coverage: global; published in 2024. Formats: CSV, ZIP, Image, TXT, NetCDF. The data are held in Consortium of Universities for the Advancement of Hydrologic Science, Inc and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 5798636858 bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is This resource is shared under the Creative Commons Attribution CC BY., taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
